title: Aftershocks

data.source: USGS ComCat earthquake catalogue: magnitude 3.0 and above within 100 km of the M 7.1 Ridgecrest earthquake of 6 July 2019, 0.5 to 365 days after it

prediction: If aftershocks were the cuts of a steadily driven count, the gaps between them would have a coefficient of variation below 1 (P1) and the average gap would not more than double from the first third to the last (P2). And the seed rule would guess the next log gap better than the Omori law (P3). We expected P1 and P2 to fail.
baseline: The Omori-Utsu law of aftershock decay, fitted on the first half, and (added after the first run) refitted as it goes; persistence; the running mean; a steady rate.
why: There was no steady count: the gaps were ragged and grew. But the seed, following recent gaps, guessed the next gap better than the Omori law fitted on the first half.
